articles.headline: Editorial Correspondence -- Our trip to Baltimore and Washington
articles.summary: Editor Weaver's correspondence recounting a Nov 20-Dec 1 preaching tour through Baltimore and Washington (Ames Chapel in Stoughton Alley, Waters' Chapel, Rev. A. Stanford's church, Georgetown), Congress and the impeachment debate, and church collections. Notes Mrs. F. E. Harper lecturing in Washington.
people: lecturer (Mrs.); lectured at Union Bethel Church, Washington D.C., Nov 27, 1867 -- Frances Ellen Watkins Harper, a Philadelphian, so linked though the event was in Washington

articles.headline: The Death of Rev. Jeremiah S. Bulaugh
articles.summary: The Rev. Jeremiah S. Bulaugh, whose death was announced in the last issue (Nov 30), was buried Friday Nov 29. The funeral procession moved from his residence in Pricketer St. to Bethel Church; after services the body was deposited in the tomb.
people: deceased (Rev.); surname and residence street uncertain on microfilm [VERIFY]
delivered the funeral discourse (Rev.), pastor of Zion Mission

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: Three marriage notices. Oct 24, 1867, by Rev. Reeve: William Henry Johnson to Elizabeth S. Hemsley (no place stated). Nov 27, 1867, by Rev. T. Gould: William Alexander Miller and Rachel Baldwin, both of Princeton, N.J. At Mount Holly, N.J., Nov 28, by Rev. Jacob Mitchell: James Herrin of Richmond, Va., to Mrs. Sarah G. Groves of Evesham, N.J.
people: groom; no place stated [VERIFY whether Philadelphia]

articles.headline: Notice -- funeral sermon of Mrs. Ann Butler
articles.summary: The funeral sermon of Mrs. Ann Butler, late of Camden, N.J., will be preached in Big Wesley Church, Lombard street, Dec. 8th, at 2 o'clock P.M.
people: deceased (Mrs.), late of Camden N.J.; funeral sermon at Big Wesley Church, Lombard St.

articles.headline: Omission (United Methodist Church)
articles.summary: Correction: in an advertisement of the United Methodist Church last week, the names of Rev. Charles Hogle, presiding elder, and Rev. Washington Stanley, minister in charge, were omitted.

articles.headline: House of Application for Colored People (James E. Griffo)
articles.summary: Mr. James E. Griffo has opened his house for the application of colored people, male or female, wishing to obtain situations in any capacity; apply at No. 904 Barclay street, Philadelphia. Persons may also board or lodge until obtaining situations. Dec. 1, 1867.
people: proprietor; employment/boarding house, No. 904 Barclay St., Philadelphia [VERIFY surname]

people: proprietor (Mrs.); employment house, No. 1718 Sansom St., Philadelphia

articles.headline: Furniture -- R. M. Adger's Housekeepers' Furnishing Store
articles.summary: R. M. Adger's Housekeepers' Furnishing Store, No. 716 Lombard St., under Liberty Hall. Dealer in all kinds of new and second-hand furniture, cooking utensils, carpets, hardware, crockery, tinware, desks, show cases, etc.; old furniture bought or exchanged; varnishing and repairing. Dated Oct. 1, 1867.

articles.headline: Dentists and Herb Doctors -- Dr. T. M. Kennard & Bro.

Kennard & Bro., Dentists and Herb Doctors, have opened their office at 832 Carpenter Street AND 747 Lombard Street, where dentistry in all its branches is attended to; Dr. Kennard also deals in botanic/herb medicines. articles.headline: A Cry for Help (Book Concern Committee appeal)
articles.summary: The Book Committee of the Book Concern of the A.M.E. Church is making every effort to raise money to meet claims before year's end; urges preachers, subscribers and agents in debt to forward what they can. Signed by the Committee.

articles.headline: Married
articles.summary: On the 5th of December, by the Rev. Frisby, Mr. Charles Downs, to Miss Mary Jane Rivers, both of Philadelphia.

articles.headline: Married

articles.headline: Died

articles.author: Mary Ann Sipple

events.name: Thanksgiving at Bethel Church
events.description: The Thanksgiving sermon at Bethel Church was preached by Rev. William Moore, from the text 'Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord' (Ps. 33:12); a collection was taken at the close. Rev. Jas. M. Williams, of Trenton, N.J., had been appointed to deliver the discourse but failed to reach the city (Williams non-Phila, text only).

events.name: Bishop Wayman's Appointments (Nov 17 - Christmas 1867)
events.location: Union, Bethel and Wesley churches, Philadelphia (and NJ/DE/MD/VA/PA points)
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's published itinerary. Sun Nov 17: morning Union church, afternoon Bethel church, night Wesley church, Philadelphia. Then Woodbury, Vineland, Gouldtown, Bridgeton, Salem N.J.; Laurel and Georgetown Del.; Salisbury Md.; Norfolk/Portsmouth, Eastville (dedication), Pocomoke Va.; Baltimore (Ebenezer, Waters', Bethel) Dec 8; Hagerstown Md.; Greencastle, Chambersburg, Reading, Deep Valley, West Chester, Oxford, Germantown Pa.; Camden, Burlington, Freehold, Bordentown, Trenton, Princeton N.J.; Christmas day Bethel church, Baltimore.

events.name: Benefit Festival for Brother Richard Young
events.location: Union Hall, Brown St. above Fourth, Philadelphia
events.description: Brother Richard Young, for years a sexton of the Union A.M.E. Church, deprived by amputation of his leg -- a committee of ladies will give a Festival for his benefit Tuesday evening Dec 17, at Union Hall, Brown St. above Fourth; admission 25 cts.
attendees: beneficiary; sexton of Union A.M.E. Church
committee (Mrs. U. T. Hallowell) [VERIFY initial, poss. Maria Hallowell]

events.name: Downingtown Circuit Quarterly Meetings
events.location: Thornville, Downingtown, Deep Valley and Centreville (Chester Co., Pa.)
events.description: Quarterly meetings of the Downingtown Circuit: Quarterly Conference at Thornville on the 21st-22d (10 A.M.); Downingtown on the 28th-29th; Deep Valley Jan 4-5; Centreville on the 11th-12th, when a protracted meeting begins. A. Till, Elder in Charge, invites brethren; take the cars at Thirteenth and Callowhill streets for Centreville.

events.name: Fair at Liberty Hall (ladies of Bethel church, for Missionary purposes)
events.description: The ladies of Bethel church and others will hold a fair for Missionary purposes during the holidays at Liberty Hall, Lombard Street, commencing December 24, 1867; season tickets 25 cents, single 10 cents, had of the committee and at the A.M.E. Book Concern. Committee: Mrs. Sarah Wilkins, President, 601 Pine St.; Mrs. Margaret Allan, Vice President, 232 Quince St.; Mrs. Tamar Martin, Treasurer, 621 Pine St.; Mrs. Ann Wine, Secretary, rear of 637 Lombard St.; Mrs. Mary Campbell, Assistant Secretary, 710 Addison St.

events.name: People's Lecture Course (for the First Colored Baptist Church, Cherry St. above 10th)
events.location: First Baptist Church, Broad and Arch Sts., Philadelphia
events.description: A lecture course for the benefit of the First Colored Baptist Church, Cherry Street above 10th. The first lecture, Thursday evening Nov 14, 1867, at the First Baptist Church, Broad and Arch Sts., by Rev. John E. Chesshire; subject 'Four months' impressions in Europe.' Tickets 25 cts., course tickets $2.00. (First lecture Nov 14; the notice ran in November too.)

events.name: Olive Union Lodge No. 2, I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria (notice)
events.description: Olive Union Lodge No. 2, I.O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, meets the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at Masonic Hall, South 11th Street, Philadelphia, at 8 o'clock. Dated Dec. 1, 1867 (no officers named).

events.name: Mass Meeting of the Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Conference (Book Concern / Christian Recorder relief)
events.description: The Preachers' Association of the Philadelphia Conference resolved to renew efforts in behalf of the Christian Recorder by holding Mass Meetings in the churches, the ministers not having generally responded to the Conference's recommendation to raise $7,000 for the relief of the Book Concern. The first meeting to be held in Bethel Church, Philadelphia, Thursday evening, December 19th. Signed T. Gould, President; H. J. Rhodes, Secretary.

events.name: Third Quarterly Conference of the Burlington Circuit
events.description: Notice: the Third Quarterly Conference of the Burlington Circuit (Philadelphia Conference, N.J.) will be held at Mount Holly, N.J., at 10 A.M. on Saturday; members requested to attend (minister's name not legible on the microfilm). Dated December 21.

ISSUE CR_1867-12-14 (Vol. VII No. 50, Whole No. 362; Weaver, Editor & Publisher, 631 Pine). Frames p1=41, p2=42, p3=43, p4=44.

PAGE 1 (frame 41) read IN FULL from crops, all 7 columns ~5 slices each: entirely devotional poems ('Longings'), out-of-town letters (Letter from North Carolina, sgd S.J., Hillsboro' N.C.; Letter from Hannibal Mo., sgd James C. Embry; Lewistown Circuit Pa., Hollidaysburg; Letter from Chicago Illinois, sgd Lewis H. Cols 5-7 advertisements, CONFIRMED FROM CROPS to be the SAME standing ads as Dec 7 (Jinnings/Empire State House, Whipper & Purnell, Dr. Armstrong, M. A. Williams boxes, Tanner's 'Apology for African Methodism', Kennard dentists, Pa. Central RR, Dr. Rosell, Dandridge Kelly/Baltimore, Charles Magarge paper, William Still coal, Bowers coal, A. Upham, Wilberforce, Newspaper Laws, Good Samaritans directory, Book Depository, Duterte, James W. Brown dyeing, Globe Hotel/Powell, Hawkins, W. P. Powell attorney, Leizeare Brown, Matlack, Longfellow, Jas. B. Rodgers) -- not re-entered.

CORRECTIONS from clearer Dec 14 impressions of standing ads: Dr. T. M. Kennard & Bro.'s second address reads 717 LOMBARD STREET (the Dec 7 tentative '747 Lombard' was a misread -- likely 717). The Good Samaritans lodge is 'SUMNER and Wilson Lodge, No. 8' (named for Charles Sumner), not 'Banner' as tentatively read Dec 7. Wm. H. Longfellow's dentist address reads 1126 Rodman Street (not 126). A. Upham confectionery reads 630 Pine St (white-owned, skip either way).

PAGE 2 (frame 42): the Philadelphia content is two Book Concern items captured above (Preachers' Association resolution + Mass Meeting at Bethel Dec 19, sgd T. Gould Pres./H. J. Rhodes Sec.; and 'A Cry for Help' committee William Moore, H. Dorrell, H. J. Rhodes). Col 1 editorial notes (Book Committee note; 'Rev. Henry Davis of New Jersey' agent; 'On the Wing'; the Freedman's Torchlight published in Brooklyn by the African Civilization Society, portrait of Fred. Douglass -- Brooklyn, note only). Also 'Letter from Providence R.I.' (Rev. John H. W. Hurley, Rev. J. Turpin -- Rhode Island, text only). Rest of p2 is out-of-town letters, fiction and recipes.

PAGE 3 (frame 43): mostly REPEATS of Dec 7 (Bishop Wayman's appointments; Downingtown Circuit/A. Till; Richard Young benefit festival; People's Lecture Course/Chesshire; Liberty Hall Fair committee -- Sarah Wilkins, Margaret Allan, Tamar Martin, Ann Wine, Mary Campbell; Olive Union Lodge No. 2; House of Application; Eliza Brooke Information Wanted; R. The House of Application proprietor (904 Barclay St.) is printed 'Mr. James B. Griffin' in the Dec 14 notice, so the surname is Griffin (the Dec 7 'James E. Griffo' reading was a misread); initial B or E uncertain.
